about.title: La Verne Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Falls happen fast, often on a wet floor, a broken step, or a cracked walkway that property owners in La Verne should have caught before someone got hurt. Whether it happened at a business along Foothill Boulevard, a rental property near White Avenue, or a shopping center off Arrow Highway, proving fault usually comes down to one question: did the owner know, or should they have known, about the hazard in time to fix it or warn you? That's where documentation matters most. Photos of the hazard, witness names, and surveillance footage can disappear or get overwritten within days, so acting quickly protects your options. We handle slip and fall and premises liability claims — we'll evaluate what happened, gather the evidence before it's gone, and explain what California's premises liability rules mean for your specific fall. There's no cost for your free case review, and no obligation to move forward.

items.title: We Understand the Notice Requirement
items.desc: California law generally requires showing the property owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard. We know how to dig for maintenance logs, prior complaints, and other proof of notice.

items.title: We Move on Evidence Before It's Gone
items.desc: Surveillance footage at stores and apartment complexes is often erased within days or weeks. Our team can send preservation requests quickly so that footage of your fall isn't lost.

items.title: We Factor in California's Comparative Fault Rule
items.desc: Because California uses pure comparative fault, you can often still recover even if you're partly blamed for the fall — your share of fault just reduces the recovery rather than eliminating it. We can help make sure your percentage of fault is argued fairly.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in La Verne?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit against a private property owner. If the fall happened on public property, such as a city sidewalk or a government building, the deadline is much shorter and involves a separate claims process. Because these timelines can be strict, it's worth contacting us soon after the fall.

items.question: What if I fell at a business along Foothill Boulevard or Arrow Highway and didn't take photos?
items.answer: Photos help, but they aren't the only evidence available. Many businesses along these corridors have interior or parking lot surveillance cameras, and we can act quickly to request that footage before it's routinely deleted. Witness statements, incident reports, and maintenance records can also fill in gaps.

items.question: Does it cost anything to get a case review?
items.answer: No. Our case reviews are free, and we generally work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. There's no obligation to move forward after we've reviewed your claim.
